name: davinci_i2s_tdm_word_length
prose: Pure mapping from a TDM slot width in bits to the McBSP word-length code: 8 gives DAVINCI_MCBSP_WORD_8, 12 gives WORD_12, 16 gives WORD_16, 20 gives WORD_20, 24 gives WORD_24, 32 gives WORD_32, and any other width returns -EINVAL. No side effects.
note: davinci-i2s.c:220-238. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits EINVAL): right; contract left empty (enum constants).

name: davinci_mcasp_set_dai_fmt
prose: Precondition: cpu_dai belongs to a davinci McASP; fmt is the DAI format word. Returns 0 without any register access if fmt is 0. Otherwise it takes a runtime PM reference (pm_runtime_get_sync, result not checked) and validates three fields in turn, each returning -EINVAL for an unsupported value: the format (DSP_A, DSP_B, AC97, I2S, RIGHT_J, LEFT_J; each sets or clears the FSXDUR/FSRDUR frame-sync duration bits and chooses a data delay of 1 for DSP_A and I2S, 0 for the others, and I2S additionally inverts the frame-sync polarity logic), the clock provider (BP_FP, BP_FC, BC_FP, BC_FC; each programs the ACLKX/ACLKR and AFSX/AFSR enable bits, the pdir pin direction bits and bclk_master), and the clock inversion (IB_NF, NB_IF, IB_IF, NB_NF; each sets or clears the ACLK polarity bits and chooses the frame-sync polarity, flipped when I2S set inv_fs), then it sets or clears the FSXPOL/FSRPOL bits and stores fmt in mcasp->dai_fmt. The data-delay fields in TXFMT and RXFMT are written after the format switch passes and before the provider is checked. On any -EINVAL the earlier register updates are not undone and mcasp->dai_fmt is not updated. Every path after the PM get, including the errors, releases the reference with pm_runtime_put and returns ret.
note: slice cut the head; real function davinci-mcasp.c:439-608. Reviewer right: an unsupported clock-provider value returns -EINVAL (562-564); the old prose omitted that validation.

name: open_patch
prose: Precondition: sflist is the soundfont list, data a user pointer to a soundfont_open_parm, count its size (unused), client the opening client id; the caller snd_soundfont_load holds the snd_soundfont_lock_preset guard on sflist (soundfont.c:119-120), while open_patch itself only takes sflist->lock briefly with irqsave. Returns 0 or a negative error. Under sflist->lock it returns -EBUSY if sflist->open_client is already set (non-negative) or sflist->currsf is non-NULL. Then it copies the parameter block from user space (-EFAULT on failure). If the patch type is a special type it ORs in SNDRV_SFNT_PAT_SHARED and creates the soundfont with newsf(sflist, type, NULL); otherwise newsf(sflist, type, parm.name). A NULL result returns -ENOMEM. Otherwise, under sflist->lock, it records the client in sflist->open_client and the new soundfont in sflist->currsf and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function soundfont.c:183-213. Reviewer right: snd_soundfont_load calls it while holding the preset lock (guard at 119), so the 'caller holds no lock' precondition was wrong.

name: snd_usb_endpoint_prepare
prose: Precondition: chip and ep are the USB audio chip and endpoint; the function takes chip->mutex itself with a scope guard (released on every return), so the caller must not already hold it. Returns 1 if the endpoint was prepared, 0 if nothing needed doing, or a negative error. It returns 0 (after a WARN_ON) if ep->iface_ref is NULL, and 0 if ep->need_prepare is false. If the interface is already set up (iface_ref->need_setup false) it only re-initialises the sample rate for UAC1 endpoints (init_sample_rate; a negative result is returned) and goes to done. Otherwise it deselects the altsetting with endpoint_set_interface(chip, ep, false) (result ignored); for UAC1 formats, or if QUIRK_FLAG_SET_IFACE_FIRST is set, it selects the interface first (a negative result is returned); then it calls snd_usb_init_pitch, init_sample_rate and snd_usb_select_mode_quirk (each negative result returned); for other formats it selects the interface last (negative result returned); it clears iface_ref->need_setup. At done it clears ep->need_prepare and returns 1.
note: slice cut the head; real function endpoint.c:1459-1524. Reviewer right: chip->mutex is acquired in this function (guard at 1465), the old claim that the caller holds it was wrong.

name: hiface_pcm_prepare
prose: Precondition: alsa_sub is a hiface PCM substream. Returns -EPIPE without taking any lock if rt->panic is set, and -ENODEV if hiface_pcm_get_substream gives NULL (checked after the panic test, still without the lock). Then it takes rt->stream_mutex with a scope guard (released on every return after this point), calls hiface_pcm_stream_stop(rt) (result ignored), clears the substream's dma_off and period_off, and, only if rt->stream_state is STREAM_DISABLED, sets the rate with hiface_pcm_set_rate(rt, alsa_rt->rate) and starts the stream with hiface_pcm_stream_start(rt), returning the first nonzero result; otherwise it returns 0 after those steps.
note: slice cut the head; real function hiface/pcm.c:406-435. Reviewer right: the mutex is taken only after the rt->panic and sub checks (418), not for the whole body.

name: ua101_probe
prose: Precondition: interface and usb_id describe an EDIROL UA-101 or UA-1000 (idProduct 0x0044) interface. Returns 0 or a negative error. It returns -ENODEV, before taking any lock, unless the interface number of the first altsetting equals interface number 0 of the model's table. From then on it holds devices_mutex through a scope guard (released at every return). It looks for a free card index (enabled and not in devices_used) and returns -ENOENT if none; calls snd_card_new (error returned) and initialises the ua101 private data (locks, lists, work, wait queues). For each of the other interfaces it finds it with usb_ifnum_to_if (missing gives -ENXIO) and claims it with usb_driver_claim_interface (failure gives -EBUSY and clears that intf pointer); then detect_usb_format, naming of the card, alloc_stream_buffers and alloc_stream_urbs for capture and playback, snd_pcm_new with playback and capture ops and vmalloc managed buffers, snd_usbmidi_create and snd_card_register. A failure in any of these after the card was created goes to probe_error, which calls free_usb_related_resources(ua, interface) and snd_card_free(card) and returns the error. On success it sets the interface data to ua, marks the card index in devices_used and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function ua101.c:1155-1292. Reviewer right: devices_mutex is taken at 1192, after the early -ENODEV return (1188-1190), so it is not held for the whole call.

name: uaudio_iommu_map_pa
prose: Precondition: uaudio_qdev is set up; mtype selects the ring type, dma_coherent the cache attribute, pa and size the physical range. Returns the IOVA at which the range is mapped, or 0 on failure (an unsigned long, 0 means failure). It computes the IOMMU protection flags with uaudio_iommu_map_prot. For MEM_EVENT_RING it uses the fixed IOVA_BASE and, if uaudio_qdev->er_mapped is already true, remembers not to map again; for MEM_XFER_RING it gets an IOVA from uaudio_get_iova on the transfer-ring allocator; for any other type it logs an error and leaves iova 0. If iova is 0 it returns 0. If no mapping is needed (event ring already mapped) it returns iova without calling the IOMMU. Otherwise it calls iommu_map(domain, iova, pa, size, prot, GFP_KERNEL); on failure it logs, releases the IOVA with uaudio_put_iova for MEM_XFER_RING only and returns 0; on success it returns iova. This function never sets er_mapped; for the event ring that flag has to be set by the caller.
note: slice cut the head; real function qc_audio_offload.c:562-606. Reviewer right: nothing in this function sets er_mapped, so for MEM_EVENT_RING it stays false unless the caller sets it.

name: fpo_init_pattern
prose: Precondition: pattern_array has room for size unsigned ints; initial_value and target_sum define the pattern. Returns nothing and does nothing if size is 0. Otherwise it sets every one of the first size elements to initial_value, computes diff = target_sum - (size * initial_value) (the product and difference are evaluated in unsigned int arithmetic, then converted to int), and then for i from 0 while i < abs(diff) it increments pattern_array[i] when diff is positive or decrements it otherwise. The loop bound is abs(diff) with no limit by size, so when |diff| exceeds size the loop writes beyond the first size elements; the function does not check this.
note: us144mkii_pcm.c:17-35. Reviewer right: the diff computation uses unsigned arithmetic (size and initial_value are unsigned int, line 28). Added observation: the loop is not bounded by size.

name: usb_stream_new
prose: Precondition: sk is the kernel-side stream state, dev the USB device, endpoints, sample_rate, use_packsize, period_frames and frame_size describe the stream; sample_rate must not be 0 (it is a divisor and is not checked). Returns sk->s, the new stream structure, or NULL on failure; at the out label it returns whatever sk->s holds, so on the paths that jump there without allocating (see below) the value is the pre-existing sk->s. It computes the packets per period from the frames per second (8000 for high speed, else 1000), rounds up to a multiple of 8 for high speed, and the read and write buffer sizes. If either size is at least 256 * PAGE_SIZE it warns and goes to out without allocating. It allocates the zeroed read buffer sk->s with alloc_pages_exact (warns and goes to out on failure, so sk->s stays NULL there) and fills its configuration (version, sample rate, frame size, period size, in-packets, read and write sizes) and sk->n_o_ps. It allocates the zeroed write buffer sk->write_page; on failure it warns, calls usb_stream_free(sk) and returns NULL. It computes sk->freqn for full or high speed. If init_urbs returns a negative value it calls usb_stream_free(sk) and returns NULL, without any warning. On success it sets the stream state to usb_stream_stopped and returns sk->s.
note: slice cut the head; real function usb_stream.c:152-236. Reviewer right: there is no warning on the init_urbs failure path (228-231).

name: usx2y_usbframe_complete
prose: Precondition: capsubs and playbacksubs are the capture and playback substreams, frame the USB frame number to submit in. Returns 0 or the first nonzero error. Playback part: it takes playbacksubs->completed_urb; if there is one, then in state STATE_RUNNING it retires it with usx2y_urb_play_retire, and in any state at or above STATE_PRERUNNING otherwise it increments the state; if there is none, then in STATE_STARTING1 it uses urb[0] and in STATE_STARTING2 urb[1], incrementing the state in both cases. If an urb was chosen it prepares it with usx2y_urb_play_prepare (using capsubs->completed_urb) and submits it with usx2y_urb_submit; either error is returned immediately, before playbacksubs->completed_urb is cleared. Otherwise it sets playbacksubs->completed_urb to NULL. Capture part: if the capture state is at least STATE_PREPARED then, in STATE_RUNNING, it retires with usx2y_urb_capt_retire (error returned), else in states at or above STATE_PRERUNNING it increments the state; it then submits capsubs->completed_urb with usx2y_urb_submit (error returned). Finally capsubs->completed_urb is set to NULL regardless of the capture state, including when the capture state is below STATE_PREPARED, and it returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function usbusx2yaudio.c:181-232. Reviewer right: line 230 clears capsubs->completed_urb outside the state test, which the old prose omitted.

name: virtsnd_ctl_query_info
prose: Precondition: snd is the virtio sound device, command the control query code, start_id and count select the entries, size is the size of one entry, info points to a buffer of at least count * size bytes for the reply; may sleep (GFP_KERNEL). It allocates a control message with virtsnd_ctl_msg_alloc (request size of struct virtio_snd_query_info, response header size) and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. It stores command, start_id, count and size in the request converted to little-endian, makes one scatter-gather entry of count * size bytes at info (the product is not checked for overflow), and returns the result of virtsnd_ctl_msg_send(snd, msg, NULL, &sg, false) (0 or a negative error); what that function does with the message on failure was not read.
note: Listed as virtsnd_ctl_query_send; the real function is virtsnd_ctl_query_info, virtio_ctl_msg.c:258-279 (slice cut the head). The old prose's claim about message ownership was not verified.

name: main
prose: Entry point of the getdelays tool (taskstats client). Options: -d, -i, -q enable delay, IO and context-switch printing; -C container path; -w log file; -r receive buffer size (negative exits via err); -m cpumask; -t tgid and -p pid (zero exits via err); -c forks and execs a command and stops option parsing; -v, -l (loop forever); any other option calls usage and exit(-1). It opens the log file if requested (exit(1) on failure), creates the generic netlink socket (err(1) on failure) and gets the taskstats family id; a zero id goes to err. It registers the cpumask if -m was given (a negative send result goes to err); selecting both -t and -C goes to err; with a forked child it waits with sigwait for SIGCHLD; if a pid/tgid is set it sends the request (a negative result goes to done); with a container it opens the path (failure goes to err) and sends the cgroupstats request (negative result goes to err); with none of cpumask, pid or container it prints usage and goes to err. It then loops receiving replies (while loop is set, or once): a negative receive length prints a message and continues the loop test; a reply with type NLMSG_ERROR or a malformed header prints 'fatal reply error' and goes to done; otherwise it walks the generic netlink attributes, printing taskstats (PID, TGID and STATS with the delay, IO and context-switch printers selected by options, writing each stats attribute to the log file if open) or cgroup stats, and when not looping goes to done after the first stats attribute. At done it deregisters the cpumask if one was registered (err(rc, ...) on a negative result). At err it closes the socket, the log file if open and the container fd if open, and returns 0. Every path that reaches the end, including the fatal reply error and the usage/early error gotos, returns 0; only the err(), usage and exit calls leave with another status.
note: slice cut the head; real function getdelays.c:355-654. Reviewer right: the fatal netlink reply error jumps to done (561) and the function returns 0 (653), it does not call err or exit.

name: #define KVM_ARM_FEATURE_ID_RANGE_IDX(op0, op1, crn, crm, op2)
prose: Function-like macro (a GNU statement expression), not a C function: it computes the index of an ID register in the feature-ID range from its system-register encoding. op0 and crn are not used. It takes __op1 = (op1) & 3 as a 64-bit value and, if that equals 3, subtracts 1 (so op1 values 0, 1, 2 and 3 map to 0, 1, 2 and 2). The result is (__op1 << 6) | (((crm) & 7) << 3) | (op2), a __u64; op2 is not masked, so a value above 7 would overlap the higher fields. Each of op1, crm and op2 is evaluated once.
note: tools/arch/arm64/include/uapi/asm/kvm.h:545-550. Previously dropped as a non-function; the macro does real arithmetic, kept as a fix with the macro head as its name. The old prose said op2 is in bits 0-2 only; the code does not mask it.

name: bpf_single_step
prose: Precondition: r is the debugger's register state (A, X, M[], Pc, R, Rs), f the instruction to execute, pkt the captured packet, pkt_caplen and pkt_len its sizes. Returns nothing; executes one classic BPF instruction by switching on f->code (K = f->k). RET with K, A or X sets r->R from K, A or X and r->Rs = true. TAX and TXA copy A to X or X to A. ST and STX store A or X into r->M[K]; LD|MEM and LDX|MEM load from r->M[K] (K is not range checked). Packet loads: for the absolute word, half-word and byte loads it computes d = pkt_caplen - K as an int and, if d >= sizeof(...) (compared as an unsigned size_t), loads A from the packet, otherwise calls set_return (which sets R to 0 and Rs true). Because d is converted to unsigned for the comparison, a K larger than pkt_caplen makes d negative, which passes the test, so such loads are not rejected and read past the captured data. The indirect loads (X + K) have the same arithmetic; the word indirect load has no else branch (A is left unchanged when the test fails), while the half-word and byte indirect loads call set_return when it fails. LDX|MSH sets X from the low nibble of the packet byte times 4 under the same test. LD|LEN sets A to pkt_len; LDX|LEN also sets A (not X) to pkt_len. IMM loads set A or X to K. JA adds K to Pc; the conditional jumps (JGT, JGE, JEQ, JSET with K or X) add f->jt or f->jf to Pc. ALU ops NEG, LSH, RSH, ADD, SUB, MUL, AND, OR and XOR update A from X or K; DIV and MOD call set_return when the divisor (X or K) is 0 and otherwise divide or take the remainder. Codes not listed leave the state unchanged.
note: slice cut the head; real function bpf_dbg.c:632-838. Reviewer right: the bounds checks mix an int difference with sizeof, so a negative d passes (lines 665-666 etc.). Added: BPF_LDX_W|BPF_LEN stores into A (line 716), as written.

name: read_kernel_config
prose: Precondition: requested_options and out_values each have num_options entries, out_values entries start as NULL for options not yet found. Returns -1 if requested_options or out_values is NULL or num_options is 0, otherwise tries to open /boot/config-<uname release> (gzopen, which also reads uncompressed files) and, if that fails or uname fails, /proc/config.gz; if neither opens it logs and returns -1 (nothing to close). It reads the first two lines with gzgets; failure to read either, or a second line that is not exactly "# Automatically generated file; DO NOT EDIT.\n", logs and sets ret to -1. If the header is good it loops over the options with read_next_kernel_config_option (which yields a name and a non-empty value per line): for each requested option it skips the option when a define_prefix is given and the option's macro_dump is not set, when its out_values entry is already non-NULL, or when the name differs; otherwise it stores strdup(value) in out_values[i] (a failed strdup is not checked and leaves NULL). The file is closed with gzclose on every path after a successful open and ret is returned: 0 when the header was valid, even if no requested option was found.
note: Listed as an unnamed config parser excerpt (dropped); the slice (bpftool/common.c:1264-1303) is the tail of read_kernel_config (1242-1303), a real function, so fixed. read_next_kernel_config_option (1214-1240) was read only at its end.

name: main
prose: Entry point of the Hyper-V fcopy UIO daemon; returns an int ret that is the process exit status (it returns, it does not call exit). ret starts as -EINVAL. Options -n (no daemon); -h or any other option prints usage and goes to exit, returning -EINVAL. If daemonizing and daemon(1, 0) fails it logs and returns -EINVAL. It then opens the log and computes the ring size; a zero size returns -ENODEV. A failed malloc of the descriptor buffer returns -ENOMEM. It opens /dev/<first uio folder> (the open failure returns the negative fd value, -1, after freeing the buffer), maps the ring buffer (on failure ret is errno, a positive number, and it closes the fd, frees the buffer and returns it), and sets up the tx and rx rings. It then loops forever: pread on the fd (a negative result with errno EINTR or EAGAIN retries; any other failure logs and goes to close, returning the negative pread result, for example -1); it receives a raw channel message (a result of 0 or less only logs); on a received message it calls fcopy_pkt_process (a negative result goes to close and is returned) and then writes to the fd to signal the host (a write that does not return sizeof(int) sets ret = errno, a positive value, logs and goes to close). The close and free_desc labels close the fd and free the buffer before returning ret.
note: slice cut the head; real function hv_fcopy_uio_daemon.c:450-559. Reviewer right: a pread failure returns the negative pread result (527-532), not a positive errno; the positive errno values come from the mmap and write-failure paths.

name: main
prose: Entry point of the Hyper-V VSS daemon. Options: -n (no daemon); -h prints usage and calls exit(0); any other option prints usage and exit(EXIT_FAILURE). If daemonizing and daemon(1, 0) fails it returns 1. At reopen_vss_fd it closes the old fd (if any); if the file system is marked frozen it tries VSS_OP_THAW and calls exit(EXIT_FAILURE) if that fails or the file system is still frozen. It opens /dev/vmbus/hv_vss (failure: exit(EXIT_FAILURE)), registers with a VSS_OP_REGISTER1 write (a negative result closes and exit(EXIT_FAILURE)), and sets in_handshake. Then it loops: poll (a negative result logs; EINVAL closes and exits with failure, other errors continue), then read. While in the handshake a read length other than sizeof(__u32) logs and exit(EXIT_FAILURE); otherwise it stores the kernel module version and ends the handshake. After the handshake a read length other than sizeof(struct hv_vss_msg) logs and goes to reopen_vss_fd (it does not exit). For FREEZE and THAW it calls vss_operate and reports HV_E_FAIL on failure, for HOT_BACKUP it only logs, for other ops it logs 'Illegal op'. It stores the error in the message and writes it back; a write whose length is not sizeof(struct hv_vss_msg) logs and goes to reopen_vss_fd. The while loop has no break, so the trailing close and exit(0) are not reached in normal operation.
note: slice cut the head; real function hv_vss_daemon.c:209-355. Reviewer right: after the handshake a wrong-size read or write goes to reopen_vss_fd (311, 349); only the handshake version read exits.

name: main
prose: Entry point of the IIO generic buffer reader; returns ret (0, a positive value left by a poll call, or a negative errno / -1). It registers cleanup and parses options (-a, -A auto channels, -b buffer index, -c loop count, -e no events, -g no trigger, -l length, -n/-N device name or number, -t/-T trigger name or number, -w delay, ? usage); a failed numeric parse sets ret = -errno and goes to error, except -T whose parse error returns -errno directly without the error cleanup, and a negative buffer index gives -ERANGE. It requires exactly one of a device number or name (else ret -1 with usage), finds the device number by name, builds the device directory name (an asprintf failure returns -ENOMEM directly) and reads the device name if only a number was given. Trigger handling: with -g none; with -T it reads the trigger name (an asprintf failure or a read failure returns directly without cleanup); otherwise it builds or looks up the trigger name (trying "<dev>-devN" then "<dev>-trigger") and goes to error if not found. It builds the channel array from sysfs (nonzero result goes to error). With auto-channels it may enable all channels and rebuild the array; if the rebuild succeeds but there are still no channels it prints a message and goes to error with ret still 0 from the rebuild, so the function returns 0 on that path. With no channels and auto-channels off it returns -ENOENT (via error). It builds the buffer directory name, checks it is a directory (-errno or -EFAULT), writes the trigger name unless -g, opens /dev/iio:deviceN non-blocking, gets the buffer fd with the ioctl, sets the buffer length, enables the buffer, computes scan_size * buf_len with an overflow check (-EFAULT), allocates the data buffer (-ENOMEM), and for buffer 0 checks that reading the device node fails with EBUSY (else -EFAULT). Then it closes the device fd and loops up to num_loops times (forever when negative): poll the buffer fd (negative result gives -errno and error; zero retries) or sleep when events are off, read the buffer (EAGAIN prints and continues, any other read error ends the loop) and call process_scan for each scan read. At error it calls cleanup, closes the fds, frees the allocated strings, data and channel names and returns ret. When the read loop ends normally ret is whatever the last poll returned (1) or, in no-events mode, the value from the earlier steps.

name: __ffs
prose: Precondition: word is expected to be nonzero. Returns the index of the least significant set bit of word (bit 0 is the least significant), computed by a binary search: with 64-bit longs it first tests the low 32 bits and, if they are all zero, adds 32 and shifts right by 32 (so words whose low 32 bits are zero return 32 to 63); then in turn it tests the low 16, 8, 4 and 2 bits, each time adding that width and shifting when the low part is zero, and finally adds 1 if bit 0 is clear. For word equal to 0 every test adds its width and the function returns 63 on 64-bit builds (31 with 32-bit longs); that value is not a valid bit index. It reads no other state and has no side effects.
note: tools/include/asm-generic/bitops/__ffs.h:14-43. Reviewer right: for 64-bit words with the low 32 bits zero the code returns 32 to 63, not 31 (lines 19-22). Contract left empty.

name: #define ffz(x)  __ffs(~(x))
prose: Function-like macro, not a C function: ffz(x) expands to __ffs(~(x)), the index of the least significant zero bit of x (the least significant set bit of its complement). It evaluates x once. If x has no zero bit (all ones in an unsigned long) the argument to __ffs is 0, for which __ffs returns 63 on 64-bit builds (31 with 32-bit longs), which is not a valid bit index. It has no state of its own.

If v is a compile-time constant that has bits outside field_mask(field), a compile-time error (__field_overflow) is raised; at run time there is no error path and out-of-range bits are dropped. field_multiplier raises a compile-time error (__bad_mask) when field is not one contiguous run of ones in the cases the compiler can evaluate; field must be non-zero, since field_mask divides by field_multiplier(field), which is 0 for field 0.

name: INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE(ITSTRUCT, ITRB, ITTYPE, ITSUBTREE, ITSTART, ITLAST, ITSTATIC, ITPREFIX)
prose: Generated function ITPREFIX_insert(node, root) (ITSTATIC, returns void): inserts an interval node into the cached rb-tree root. It starts from the root link with start = ITSTART(node), last = ITLAST(node) and leftmost = true, and walks down: at each node on the path it raises that node's ITSUBTREE to last if it is smaller, and goes left when start < ITSTART(parent), otherwise goes right and clears leftmost. It then sets node->ITSUBTREE = last, links the node at the found position with rb_link_node and rebalances with rb_insert_augmented_cached using the template's _augment callbacks. No return value; no locking is done here; node must not already be in a tree.

name: INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE(ITSTRUCT, ITRB, ITTYPE, ITSUBTREE, ITSTART, ITLAST, ITSTATIC, ITPREFIX)
prose: Generated function ITPREFIX_subtree_search(node, start, last) (static): searches the subtree rooted at node for the leftmost interval that intersects [start, last], where a node intersects if ITSTART(node) <= last and start <= ITLAST(node). The loop invariant is start <= node->ITSUBTREE. It first descends into the left child if that child's subtree can still satisfy start <= its ITSUBTREE. Otherwise, if ITSTART(node) <= last it returns node when start <= ITLAST(node), else moves to the right child when one exists and its ITSUBTREE is at least start; in every remaining case it returns NULL. It returns a pointer to the matching node or NULL, and modifies nothing.

name: #define my_syscall0(num)
prose: Function-like macro (a GNU statement expression), not a C function, for the m68k nolibc: my_syscall0(num) puts num in register d0 (as a long), executes the "trap #0" system-call instruction with d0 as input and output, with a memory clobber, and its value is the contents of d0 afterwards (the kernel's return value, a negative errno on failure).
